mentions.name: The Mandating Honeypots Project
mentions.description: This project demonstrates that age-verification via the Linux D-Bus interface can be trivially defeated: a simple Python script anyone can copy and paste makes the D-Bus interface always report 18+, rendering such checks useless. It argues the only reason to want ID verification is as a surveillance honeypot, and proposes a heavily redundant password-protected tool parents could use to keep kids from tampering with the verification service. Planned follow-ups include a mobile device version, an ID-database-focused version, and possibly a Windows version once the 'GetUserAgeRangeAsync' API ships.
mentions.problem: Age verification that asks the D-Bus interface is useless because anyone can tell it to always report 18+; the real driver for ID verification would be mass surveillance (a 'honeypot'), and governments justify it as 'for the kids'.
mentions.audience: Parents (users of the proposed tamper-protection tool)
mentions.source_excerpt: I put together this thing I call The Mandating Honeypots Project and it shows how anyone with an internet connection and copy + paste skills can trick Linux D-Buses with a simple Python script, proving that if companies want to verify your age by asking the D-Bus interface, it's easy to just tell it to always send 18+, making the whole thing useless.
mentions.author: ToriTech
